title: Account Review Deck — Micro + Extended Templates
content:
Purpose: Provide two compact, plug-and-play QBR deck outlines for Customer Success reps: a Micro QBR (15-20 minute cadence for healthy accounts or check-ins) and an Extended Enterprise QBR (45-60 minutes for strategic or at-risk accounts). These are intentionally modular so slides can be added/removed depending on maturity of the relationship and renewal timeline.

Micro QBR (15-20 minutes) — use when account is healthy, renewal > 3 months out, or for lightweight cadence
- Objective: Keep the customer informed, surface blockers early, reinforce value and usage trends, and flag any emerging risks.
- Suggested duration: 15-20 minutes (10 min presentation + 5-10 min Q&A)
- Slide flow (single page notes for each slide):
  1) Title & Agenda (30s) — Account, date, attendees, meeting goal.
  2) Quick Wins since last call (2 min) — 3 bullets: measurable wins, tickets resolved, feature releases used.
  3) Usage Snapshot (3 min) — 2 graphs: tokens/requests trend (30d), latency/cost anomalies. Note: include one-liner interpretation.
  4) Health Signals & Simple Risk Score (2 min) — short list: active seats, API error rate, feature adoption, NPS if available. Provide a single-line risk assessment: Green/Yellow/Red + reason.
  5) Tactical Ask & Next Steps (1 min) — 1-2 asks (e.g., schedule technical review, approve a pilot).
  6) Renewal/Timeline Reminder (1 min) — upcoming renewal window and any early-discount opportunities.
  7) Open Qs / Parking Lot (1–2 min) — capture follow-ups and owners.
- Speaker notes style: write a 1-2 sentence script for each slide. Keep it conversational and action-oriented.

Extended Enterprise QBR (45-60 minutes) — use when account is strategic, renewal < 6 months, or multiple stakeholders involved
- Objective: Align execs on value, identify gaps vs. outcomes, present renewal proposal roadmap, and secure a follow-up commitment (technical or commercial).
- Suggested duration: 45–60 minutes (presentation + structured discussion)
- Slide flow (with notes and time allocation):
  1) Cover + Attendees + Outcome (2 min) — clarify the decision owners and desired outcome of this session.
  2) Executive TL;DR — 1 slide (3 min) — 3 bullets: value delivered, top risk, ask. Designed for executive attendees who may only see this slide.
  3) Business Outcomes & KPIs (6–8 min) — map Redwood metrics to customer outcomes: latency improvement, cost-per-token, uptime, ML feature usage, retention impact. Include a 12-week trend and commentary on variance to target.
  4) Adoption & Usage Deep-dive (8–10 min) — breakdown by product area: hosted API, dedicated capacity, private deployment usage. Highlight power-users, unused features, and integration points. Use a callout for opportunities to reduce unit costs (caching, batching).
  5) Quality & Reliability Review (5–7 min) — incidents since last review, RCA summaries, mitigation actions, SLO attainment. Include an explicit ask: Do you want enforced SLAs or revised escalation paths?
  6) Risk & Renewal Health (5 min) — a short renewal risk matrix by stakeholder (technical, procurement, finance). Provide an aggregated risk score and the primary drivers.
  7) Commercial & Packaging Options (6–8 min) — 3 alternatives: Standard renewal terms, Value-based upsell (features + extended support), and Dedicated reserved capacity commitment. Add indicative pricing ranges and required timelines for discounts.
  8) Execution Roadmap & Dependencies (4–6 min) — 90-day plan with owners: technical runway, success milestones, exec touchpoints, and legal/contract steps.
  9) Ask & Decision Framework (3 min) — propose next steps and desired commitments (e.g., schedule procurement sync, signature timeline).
  10) Q&A + Parking Lot (5–10 min)
- Appendices (post deck slides to include as attachments if requested): product telemetry snapshots, incident timelines, SSO/KMS checklist, pilot results, feature adoption heatmaps.

Renewal Tracker (compact table you can paste into a spreadsheet) — single-line formats so they copy into sheets easily
- Columns (as simple headings you can paste into a sheet): Account, RenewalDate, ARR, Owner, DecisionOwner, RiskLevel, TopRiskReason, NextMilestone, NextMilestoneDate, ProposedOffer, LastContact, ActionItems
- Example rows (CSV-friendly single lines):
  RedwoodCo,2026-08-15,350000,Aisha Patel,CTO - Javier S.,Yellow,Procurement timeline unknown,Technical review,2026-04-02,Reserved capacity discount (10%),2026-03-01,"Schedule pre-RFP call; capture SOW changes"
  AcmeAI,2026-06-01,125000,Liam Chen,Head of ML - Priya N.,Green,Low,Usage review,2026-03-15,Standard renewal,2026-02-20,"Confirm renewal contact; send draft quote"

Renewal Playbook (sequence of plays with sample templates and owners)
- Play 0: Early Detection (Owner: CSM) — Weekly dashboard check: token trends, error rate, top apps. If RiskLevel transitions to Yellow or higher, open a Renewal Task in JIRA (template: JIRA-CS-RENEW-<account>).
- Play 1: Technical Health Sync (Owner: Solutions Eng) — Within 30–90 days of renewal, schedule 60-min technical review. Deliverable: runbook for latency/cost optimizations and a remediation plan for any open incidents.
- Play 2: Executive Alignment (Owner: CSM + Sales AE) — 6–10 weeks before renewal for mid-size and enterprise. Deliverable: executive slide (TL;DR), one-pager with ROI.
- Play 3: Commercial Negotiation (Owner: AE + RevOps) — Present 2 commercial paths: renew-as-is, or commit to reserved capacity for 6/12/24 months with graduated discounts. Include clear timelines for discount eligibility.
- Play 4: Legal & Procurement (Owner: Legal + Customer Procurement) — Start early for complex SOW changes. Maintain a shared contract checklist (SSO, IP, data residency, audit logs).
- Play 5: Win / Close / Transition (Owner: CSM) — Capture lessons in a short retro doc, update support handoff, and schedule success plan kickoff.

Operational Checklists (quick copyable items)
- Prior to QBR: verify account telemetry (last 30d), export usage chart PNGs, confirm attendees and decision owner, prepare 1-pager ROI.
- During QBR: timebox the agenda, surface one primary ask, record decisions in meeting notes, confirm next step date and owner.
- Post QBR: update renewal tracker row, open follow-up tasks (JIRA/Confluence links), send recap email within 24 hours with slide deck and action items.

Sample Email Templates (short, ready to paste)
- Executive invite subject: "[Customer] — Executive review of outcomes & renewal planning (30 min)"
  Body: "Hi <Name>, we'd like to invite you to a 30-min executive review to align on outcomes and renewal options. Proposed dates: <dates>. Objective: share 12-week value, discuss renewal timeline, and confirm next steps. Please let us know which date works best. Thanks — <CSM>"
- Technical invite subject: "[Customer] — Technical health review (60 min)"
  Body: "Hi <Name>, looking to schedule a technical session to review latency, cost, and integration points ahead of renewal. Deliverable: runbook and recommended optimizations. Proposed dates: <dates>. — <SE>"
- Post-meeting recap subject: "[Customer] QBR recap + agreed next steps"
  Body: "Thanks for the time today. Attached are the slides and the actions we agreed. Next step: <owner> to deliver <work> by <date>. Please add anything I missed. — <CSM>"

Customization guidance (how to pick slides based on account stage)
- Healthy / Micro: use only the Micro QBR slides + Renewal Tracker line + one slide for opportunities. Keep it light and cadence-driven.
- Growing / Mid-market: blend Micro + 2–3 Extended slides (Usage Deep-dive, Commercial Options, Roadmap). Add a short one-pager ROI.
- Strategic / Enterprise: use the full Extended QBR, include appendices, and schedule pre-work with engineering and procurement. Ensure legal is looped early.

Variant Suggestions (quick swaps to tailor tone)
- Customer-led tone: emphasize case studies, customer success stories, and co-sell opportunities.
- Product-led tone: emphasize feature adoption, telemetry, and roadmap influences.
- Risk-mitigation tone: prioritize incidents, SLOs, and commit to remediation timelines.

Attachments to include in drive with each deck (checklist)
- Latest usage PNGs, incident RCA PDF, proposed commercial term sheet (redlined), decision owner contacts, one-pager ROI.

Open questions / TODOs for this template set (notes)
- Add a one-page churn-risk heatmap visual (UX needed from design).
- Create a short Notion/Confluence macro to auto-pull last 30-day usage charts into the deck.
- Collect 3 anonymized customer case wins to use as optional slides.

Quick implementation notes for CSMs and SEs
- Keep slides lightweight: single insight per slide and an actionable ask.
- Always end with a named next step and date.
- For enterprise renewals, draft the proposed SOW changes before the exec review so procurement has concrete language.

Appendix: Short example of a filled Renewal Tracker entry (single-line human readable)
- Account: RedwoodCo | Renewal: 2026-08-15 | ARR: $350k | Owner: Aisha Patel | Decision Owner: Javier S. (CTO) | Risk: Yellow — procurement timeline unknown | Next milestone: Technical review 2026-04-02 | Offer: 10% reserved capacity | Actions: schedule procurement sync, deliver runbook

End of template doc. Use freely and adapt for account context. If you modify, please update linked_artifacts and reference JIRA tickets created for renewals.
